channel.description: Ecommerce news briefed in two sentences, with a link to whoever reported it.

item.title: Walmart opens fifth automated fulfillment center in Stockton, California
item.description:
Walmart has opened its fifth high-tech fulfillment center, a 900,000-square-foot facility in Stockton, California, to increase online order processing and improve West Coast delivery times. The site uses a high-density storage and retrieval system that condenses the traditional 12-step fulfillment process into five steps. E-commerce now accounts for 23% of Walmart’s total sales, and the retailer says faster delivery helps drive more online purchases.
Walmart Fulfillment Services will also operate the center to handle orders placed by third-party sellers on its Marketplace platform. Located in California’s Central Valley, the facility places inventory closer to West Coast shoppers, enabling quicker shipping options on millions of items while reducing strain on other fulfillment centers in the network. Walmart already runs four comparable next‑generation centers in Joliet, Illinois; McCordsville, Indiana; Greencastle, Pennsylvania; and Lancaster, Texas, which together support next‑day or two‑day delivery to 95% of the U.S. population. The company announced in August that it will build a sixth ultra‑modern hub in Carnesville, Georgia, covering 1.5 million square feet, with construction slated to begin later this year and a total investment of $1.3 billion.
Before the Stockton opening, Walmart operated four next‑generation fulfillment centers in the Midwest and East Coast, aiming to reach 95% of Americans with next‑day or two‑day shipping. The retailer reported that e‑commerce sales made up 23% of its total revenue, highlighting the importance of speedy fulfillment for its online growth.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/walmart-activates-automated-e-commerce-logistics-center-in-california)

item.title: eFormed Ventures buys 1898-founded Outdoor Life to launch AI gear marketplace
item.description:
eFormed Ventures acquired the 1898-founded hunting and camping magazine Outdoor Life from Recurrent Ventures. It plans to transform the title into an AI-driven outdoor gear marketplace that will sell products from outside retailers.
Outdoor Life currently earns revenue through affiliate links, but eFormed intends to operate its own store selling gear from external brands. The company will retain the magazine's editorial staff, whose product reviews and field tests will populate the marketplace. The platform will be powered by eFormed's proprietary AI system, Resonance 2.0, which recommends gear based on a shopper's location, season, browsing history, and past purchases. Resonance 2.0 aims to match users with products and prices tailored to their context.
Source: Shopifreaks (https://shopifreaks.com/eformed-ventures-acquires-outdoor-life-from-recurrent-ventures-to-turn-the-magazine-into-an-ai-powered-outdoor-gear-marketplace)

item.title: Paytm's lending revenue jumps to ₹2,594 Cr as payments growth slows
item.description:
In FY26, Paytm's financial services distribution reached ₹2,594 Cr, accounting for 31% of its ₹8,437 Cr topline, as the firm returned to profit with a net gain of ₹552 Cr. In Q1 FY27, operating revenue climbed 28% to ₹2,448 Cr and merchant GMV rose 31% to ₹7.1 lakh Cr, signalling continued momentum.
Payment services remained the largest segment at 58% of revenue, expanding at a 19% CAGR between FY21 and FY26. Paytm exited entertainment ticketing, scaled back e‑commerce ambitions and sharpened its focus on payments and financial services. Payment processing margins stayed above four basis points and subscription merchant deployments reached 1.57 crore storefronts. Paytm offsets the lack of UPI fees by offering merchant loans, insurance and point‑of‑sale device subscriptions. Paytm's super app approach now targets active payments users and merchants instead of chasing every consumer.
Paytm started as a digital wallet, expanded into a payments leader powered by UPI, and two years ago pivoted to lending after facing challenges with its payments bank. The move lifted Paytm to a net profit of ₹552 Cr in FY26, reversing a ₹663 Cr loss the prior year. Plans to introduce a 0.4% MDR fee on high‑value UPI transactions have been delayed, leaving the zero‑MDR framework in place.
Source: Inc42 (https://inc42.com/features/payments-vs-lending-the-tale-of-paytms-two-engines)

item.title: West Coast container rates slip $2 per FEU as trans-Pacific prices ease
item.description:
Far East‑U.S. West Coast spot rates fell $2 per FEU on Oct. 7, marking the first daily decline in weeks. Despite the drop, rates stayed 1.1% above their Sept. 30 level at $8,336 per FEU, while Asia‑U.S. East Coast averages rose to $11,512 per FEU, up 0.5% over the week. On the trans‑Atlantic lane, North Europe‑U.S. East Coast spot rates slipped 1.1% week over week to $2,854 per FEU.
Asia‑Mediterranean spot rates averaged $4,007 per FEU, down 5.9% from Sept. 30. Lower short‑term rates are giving European shippers more leverage as they negotiate long‑term contracts. The narrowing gap between Mediterranean and North Europe rates reflects shifting trade patterns.
“For European shippers, tender season is in full force and falling short-term rates are a welcome development as they negotiate long-term contracts,” Peter Sand, Chief Analyst at Xeneta said.
As demand eases from a high level, competition for vessel capacity is diminishing, improving negotiating conditions for shippers. Sand said carrier rerouting away from the Suez Canal route around Africa may help explain the pricing relationship.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/us-west-coast-container-rates-edge-lower)

item.title: Truckload rates rise in 2026 as capacity exits market faster than freight
item.description:
Truckload rates rose in 2026 as carriers exited the market faster than freight demand grew. The average cost to operate a truck reached a record $2.336 per mile in 2025, according to ATRI’s Operational Costs of Trucking study. Spot linehaul rates remained below non‑fuel costs every year from 2023 through 2025, while contract linehaul gradually recovered.
Contract linehaul rates averaged $2.69 per mile in Q3 2026, still below Q4 2021 levels and having rebuilt only about half the profit cushion carriers enjoyed in 2022. Tolls rose 13.2%, repair and maintenance 8.6%, driver benefits 6.6% and tires 6.4%, setting records across nearly every cost line. Tender rejections have surged, with the STRI up 268% since October 2023 while tender volume rose only about 9%, and for‑hire tractor counts fell by roughly 51,000 in a single month. To cover overhead, rates would need to be about 14% higher than current benchmark levels, and even running near the hours‑of‑service ceiling a typical truck still falls about 5% short.
Carriers spent three years hauling at rates that barely covered their costs, often falling short in the spot market. The 2026 rate increase is described as a correction that is only about halfway done. In 2022, dry van contract linehaul averaged $2.81 per mile, but by 2024‑2025 it had fallen to $2.32 while non‑fuel costs rose roughly 30% from 2021 to 2025.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/why-trucking-rates-are-rising-without-more-freight)

item.title: AAFA Urges USTR to Add Facebook, Instagram to 2026 Notorious Markets List
item.description:
The American Apparel and Footwear Association asked the Office of the United States Trade Representative to place Facebook, Instagram, Alibaba.com, AliExpress and DHGate on its 2026 Review of Notorious Markets for Counterfeiting and Piracy. The association said its recommendation reflects data from its membership of 1,100 brands and retailers across the fashion space.
Lamar said counterfeiters use online platforms to deceive consumers with fraudulent listings that mimic trusted brands and may contain hazardous chemicals. He added that a February 2025 study found 41 percent of 39 lab‑tested products failed international safety standards. AAFA noted that brands cannot police counterfeits alone and must constantly monitor marketplaces, a whack‑a‑mole effort many lack bandwidth for.
“Counterfeiters increasingly use online platforms to deceive consumers with fraudulent listings that mimic trusted brands to sell products that fail to meet basic safety standards and may contain hazardous chemicals or other dangerous substances,” Steve Lamar, president and CEO, AAFA said.
Commercial fraud and the sale of duped fashion products are on the rise, and the American Apparel and Footwear Association is urging the federal government to take action against online platforms it believes pose the greatest threat to the market. The proliferation of dupes and fakes across online platforms like Facebook and Instagram is undercutting U.S. fashion brands and endangering consumers, the group said.
Source: WWD (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/industry-news/aafa-meta-facebook-instagram-ustr-2026-notorious-markets-review-counterfeits-1239334279)

item.title: NeoGrowth secures ₹85 crore to boost digital lending for Indian MSMEs
item.description:
NeoGrowth has raised ₹85 crore ($8.8 million) in a debt‑and‑equity round led by FMO with LeapFrog Investments participating. The proceeds will fund expansion of its digital lending platform, deepen market presence across India, and increase credit access for micro, small, and medium enterprises.
The platform manages nearly ₹2,000 crore in assets under management and has served more than 400,000 businesses to date.
NeoGrowth previously raised ₹300 crore in equity in 2022, with FMO contributing over half of that round. Existing backers include Omidyar Network, Lightrock, Khosla Impact, Accion Frontier Inclusion Fund–Quona Capital and 360 ONE Asset.
Source: Inc42 (https://inc42.com/buzz/neogrowth-raises-%E2%82%B985-cr-to-expand-digital-lending-capabilities)

item.title: Tesco anticipates shoppers will reduce alcohol purchases this Christmas
item.description:
Tesco expects shoppers to cut back on alcohol this Christmas and has expanded its online grocery delivery capacity by 10% for the peak trading period. Chief executive Ken Murphy said customers are increasingly opting for low‑ and no‑alcohol alternatives such as ready‑mixed mocktails as part of a wider shift toward healthier lifestyles.
Tesco has increased its stock of key Christmas products and expanded its online grocery delivery capacity by 10% ahead of the peak trading period. The retailer is also investing in its rapid delivery service Whoosh and has signed new partnerships, including with Deliveroo, to meet demand for convenience. Tesco's premium Finest range sales rose 9% in the first half of the year, while first‑half sales increased 2% to £33.8 billion and adjusted operating profit climbed 6.5% to £1.78 billion, leading to an upgraded full‑year profit forecast of between £3.15 billion and £3.3 billion. Despite the move toward lower‑alcohol choices, Tesco anticipates that shoppers will continue to spend on festive treats such as chocolates, mince pies and party foods.
“I do think it could be a marginally healthier Christmas although customers do love to indulge,” Ken Murphy, Chief Executive said.
The shift toward lower‑alcohol choices has been developing since the pandemic, initially driven by younger consumers before spreading to older age groups. Murphy noted that the growing popularity of weight‑loss drugs has been cited as a key factor, though he said it is only one element behind broader changes in consumer habits.
Source: Grocery Gazette (https://grocerygazette.co.uk/2026/10/09/tesco-expects-shoppers-to-cut-back-on-alcohol-this-christmas)

item.title: Tesco boss urges Chancellor to exempt retailers from higher warehouse tax
item.description:
Tesco chief executive Ken Murphy urged Chancellor John Healey to exempt retailers from higher business rates on large warehouses as the supermarket reported its half-year results on Thursday. He said retailers are paying four times more than their fair share of rates and called for more equitable taxation.
Murphy called for an exemption for retail businesses from the higher business rates multiplier applied to properties with a rateable value above £500,000. Savills research showed high street retailers occupied 97 million square feet of warehouse space in 2024, compared with 69 million square feet used by online retailers. Tesco upgraded its full-year profit guidance, now expecting adjusted operating profit between £3.15 billion and £3.3 billion for the year to February 2027, up from a previous forecast of £3 billion to £3.3 billion. UK like-for-like sales rose 1.5 percent in the 26 weeks to 29 August, while group adjusted operating profit reached £1.78 billion.
“Retailers are paying four times more than their fair share of rates and I would urge the Government for more equitable rates,” Ken Murphy, Tesco CEO said.
“We genuinely believe rates need to be reformed and we urge the Government to exempt retailers from the threshold put in place last year,” Ken Murphy, Tesco CEO said.
The government is considering increasing the tax burden on large warehouses and out-of-town properties to fund business rates reductions for smaller high street businesses such as pubs and live music venues. Retailers have warned that the changes would disproportionately affect traditional high street businesses that operate extensive distribution networks, and analysis shows the highest business rates bills belong to warehouses run by Lidl, Tesco, John Lewis, Sainsbury’s and Marks & Spencer.
Source: Grocery Gazette (https://grocerygazette.co.uk/2026/10/09/tesco-boss-urges-chancellor-to-spare-retailers-from-unfair-warehouse-tax)

item.title: KISAH raises ₹35.9 Cr to scale retail footprint
item.description:
KISAH raised ₹35.9 Cr in a Series A funding round led by Fireside Ventures. The round values the Kolkata-based menswear brand at around ₹211 Cr post-money. Cofounder Yash Sarawagi said the funds will help create retail playbooks, with franchisees financing further expansion.
The startup intends to use the capital primarily to expand its retail network, while also investing in supply chain, warehousing, technology and backend infrastructure to support omnichannel operations. Prior to this round, KISAH had raised around ₹10 Cr from angel investors such as Wow! Momo founder Sagar Daryani and Salarpuria Group's Apoor Salarpuria, who also contributed strategic guidance. The brand, founded in 2018 by Yash Sarawagi, now operates 12 stores across Bengaluru, Kolkata, Hyderabad, Mumbai and Visakhapatnam, with the Kolkata Gariahat outlet generating ₹45-50 lakh in its first partial year and about ₹70 lakh annually. KISAH reports FY26 revenue of ₹65 Cr with an EBITDA margin of 5-6% and targets ₹100 Cr revenue in FY27, implying about 70% growth, while projecting the offline business to grow four-fivefold and contribute 25-30% of total sales.
“We are learning retail right now. We've had very good positive early signs for us. The idea is that we are using this money to create our playbooks, and then the retail expansion is something which should be funded by franchisees,” Yash Sarawagi, cofounder said.
KISAH began as a marketplace-led brand before launching its own D2C platform and opening physical stores. The company's first offline store opened in Kolkata's Gariahat in 2025, generating ₹45-50 lakh in its partial year and about ₹70 lakh annually thereafter. Prior to the Series A, the startup had secured roughly ₹10 crore from angel investors including Wow! Momo's Sagar Daryani and Salarpuria Group's Apoor Salarpuria.
Source: Inc42 (https://inc42.com/buzz/menswear-brand-kisah-nets-%E2%82%B935-9-cr-to-scale-retail-footprint)

item.title: Colruyt Group confirms exclusive talks with Carrefour over Codifrance sale
item.description:
Colruyt Group confirmed it is in exclusive negotiations with Carrefour over a potential sale of its French wholesale subsidiary Codifrance. Carrefour is reportedly considering offering 155 million euros for Codifrance, though no guarantee exists that an agreement will be reached.
Codifrance supplies dry goods, fresh products, and frozen foods to more than 800 affiliated stores under its own brands—Panier Sympa, Épi Service, and VivÉco—as well as the licensed brands Coccinelle and Coccimarket. It also serves roughly 2,200 independent retailers across about three-quarters of France. After acquiring Degrenne Distribution in July 2023, Codifrance’s revenue reached approximately 310 million euros in the 2025/26 fiscal year, while Colruyt had already sold its French integrated retail operations several months earlier.
Earlier rumors of a possible sale were dismissed by the companies as a rumor, but Colruyt Group later confirmed it is in exclusive negotiations with Carrefour regarding the sale of its French subsidiary Codifrance. Colruyt Group had previously sold its French integrated retail operations several months before these talks began.
Source: RetailDetail EU (https://retaildetail.eu/news/food/colruyt-group-confirms-talks-with-carrefour-regarding-french-wholesaler-codifrance)

item.title: Hai Robotics seeks Hong Kong listing after 2025 revenue tops RMB2.02 billion
item.description:
Hai Robotics refreshed its Hong Kong listing application on September 13, aiming to build on 2025 revenue of RMB2.02 billion. Sales outside mainland China made up more than half of its revenue in the first half of 2026.
Founded in 2016, the Shenzhen‑based firm makes robots that retrieve individual containers from warehouse racks and bring them to workstations, allowing aisles to narrow and workers to stay at picking stations. Its newer machines climb the racks themselves, turning height into storage capacity without requiring workers to follow inventory upward. Goldman Sachs and CITIC Securities are joint sponsors of the listing, and research for the filing ranked Hai as the world’s largest provider of autonomous case‑handling robot solutions by revenue and shipments in 2025. The company says turning successful warehouse projects into a profitable global business is its next challenge.
Warehouse automation has long relied on conveyors, cranes and automated storage systems, with more recent mobile robots moving shelves or containers across floors. Hai Robotics focused on the individual case, introducing a single‑case robot system in 2017 and a multi‑case version in 2018. Its goods‑to‑person approach sends inventory to workers instead of requiring them to travel to inventory.
Source: TechNode (https://technode.com/2026/10/09/the-robots-taking-warehouses-to-new-heights)

item.title: Tesco names Kingfisher’s Chris Blatchford as new CTO effective March 2027
item.description:
Tesco has appointed Chris Blatchford, currently Group CTO at Kingfisher, as its Chief Technology Officer and executive committee member starting March 2027. He succeeds Guus Dekkers, who is retiring in December after eight years with the retailer, while Tesco’s Technology Director Jane Mustoe will serve as acting CTO from November 2026.
Blatchford will lead Tesco’s technology, data and digital transformation teams, reporting directly to the chief executive and sitting on the executive committee. At Kingfisher he oversaw the IT infrastructure and digital platforms for the B&Q, Screwfix, Castorama, and Brico Dépôt banners, managing large‑scale systems across multiple European markets. Tesco’s outgoing CTO Dekkers is credited with building an outstanding technology organisation that has supported the retailer’s strategic ambitions over his eight‑year tenure. Ken Murphy, Tesco’s Group Chief Executive, said Blatchford’s experience in scaling technology operations and building high‑performing teams will help strengthen the role of technology in serving customers and supporting long‑term growth. Blatchford has said he looks forward to working with the team to build on the momentum established under Dekkers’ leadership and continue delivering technology that makes a real difference for customers, colleagues, and the business.
“There are so many opportunities for technology to improve the experience for customers and colleagues across the Tesco ecosystem,” Chris Blatchford, Chief Technology Officer said.
“Chris has led technology, data and digital transformation at scale and brings a combination of strategic vision, deep technical expertise and a strong track record of building high performing teams,” Ken Murphy, Group Chief Executive said.
